hypothesis: In a large measured cross-sectional sample, the coefficient of variation (CV) of human stature and of weight, computed by single year of age and by sex, falls as the growth rate falls in childhood and rises again through the adolescent growth spurt, so CV covaries positively with growth velocity.
pass_criterion: Using NHANES examination-sample weights, compute the CV (SD/mean) of standing height and of weight for each single year of age 2-19, separately for males and females. Estimate growth velocity v(a) = [mean(a+1) - mean(a-1)]/2 for ages 3-18. The claim passes only if, for stature and for weight, in both sexes (4 tests): (i) Spearman rho between CV(a) and v(a) across ages 3-18 is >= 0.50; and (ii) the CV has a minimum at an age <= 10 and then rises by >= 10% of the minimum value at some age between 11 and 15. All four tests must meet both conditions. The pre-registered inference is a bootstrap (PSU resampling) 95% CI lower bound for rho above 0.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if, in any of the four sex-by-measure tests, rho < 0.30, or its bootstrap 95% CI includes 0. It is also refuted if there is no post-minimum rise of at least 10% in CV at ages 11-15. In that case the CV is not a function of growth rate as stated. A rho between 0.30 and 0.50 counts as inconclusive, not as a pass.
interpretation: Thompson's 'coefficient of variability' is the CV, SD/mean, of stature and of weight at each age. His 'rate of growth' is the annual increment in mean stature or weight. His data were Boas's and Bowditch's cross-sectional school surveys. Here the increment is taken from successive age-specific cross-sectional means, since NHANES is not longitudinal. The modern reinterpretation is that measured NHANES height (BMXHT) and weight (BMXWT) replace his school measurements. Single years of age (RIDAGEYR) replace his age groups. Sex is RIAGENDR. His statement is qualitative ('a function of'), so a monotone positive association (Spearman) plus the dip-then-rise shape is the operational test. Because 'not yet in a position to equate the terms precisely', no functional form is tested. The test is limited to the growth years 2-19, as in his discussion.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
dataset.publisher: CDC National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS)
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES is a nationally representative survey in which stature and weight are measured, not self-reported, in the mobile examination centre. The Examination component's Body Measures file (BMX) gives standing height (BMXHT, cm) and weight (BMXWT, kg). The Demographics file (DEMO) gives age (RIDAGEYR), sex (RIAGENDR), the exam weight (WTMEC2YR) and the design variables SDMVPSU and SDMVSTRA. Pooled cycles give large samples per single year of age and sex. The data are downloadable as SAS transport files through the NHANES data pages linked from this landing page. The landing page was fetched and does not itself list files, so file-level names such as BMX and DEMO are taken from my knowledge of NHANES and should be confirmed on the data-release pages.
